The repository contains no plot script, table generator, LaTeX/TikZ source, or matching data file for the other PDF objects.

source_acquisition.search_note: The inventory row reports no_public_source_found and corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-f46849c406ca/ is absent. The PDF abstract is the direct link to https://github.com/WillDreamer/T2PO. Read-only gh metadata confirms the exact README title “T^2PO: Uncertainty-Guided Exploration Control for Stable Multi-Turn Agentic RL”, arXiv:2605.02178, and default-branch commit 4dc21d78d3312af45bbe651cb061d1abe7d27840 (2026-05-27). A recursive tree search found public/main.png and unrelated public/ARL.png plus no figure/plot/table/LaTeX source; only public/main.png is a verified visual match for Figure 2. Thus the source state is partial_visual_source, with Figure 1/3–7 and Tables 1–8 audited from the verified PDF render and PDF text objects.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures use local categorical roles—blue/orange method comparisons, red/blue/purple seed or budget settings, green uncertainty traces, and pale fills for variation—with no paper-wide color key. Tables remain mostly monochrome booktabs/partial-grid layouts, using gray or light group separation and bold proposed/best cells.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: At 200 dpi, all seven figures are embedded raster image objects (Figure 2 includes a soft-mask raster); captions, surrounding prose, table text, and table rules are PDF text/vector objects. The PDF therefore mixes raster figures with vector/text tables. The only source asset found is the README-linked raster public/main.png for Figure 2.
paper_style.style_consistency: The PDF’s body, captions, equations, and tables consistently use Nimbus Roman and Computer Modern families, while raster figures contain Times-like labels, monospaced token examples, and varied palette conventions. Caption labels are italic and table grouping/bold conventions are stable, but legend placement, scale treatment, and figure color roles vary by object.

figures.evidence_relation: Introduction failure claim → insufficient exploration/hesitation diagnosis → T2PO token- and turn-level controls in Section 4 → Figure 5 stable training comparison and Tables 1–4 results/ablations.
design_strengths: Aligns performance collapse with two internal diagnostics rather than showing only one outcome.
Repeating three seeds and using both marker and line-style roles makes baseline identity inspectable.

Small legends and mixed y units limit quantitative comparison; it motivates but cannot identify which method component causes the collapse.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a horizontally matched outcome–diagnostic–diagnostic triptych, with repeated seeds and a restrained background annotation, to motivate a failure mode before introducing a control method.

caption.text: Figure 5. We evaluate both task performance and exploration efficiency. (a) shows that T²PO enables performance to steadily improve without collapse on three different env seeds. design_weaknesses: Mixed numeric scales across prompting/SFT/RL rows make visual comparisons invalid without normalization.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes baseline training collapse (success falls as KL and gradient norms rise); Figure 2 supplies the rollout/TTI/TDS interface; Figure 3 motivates the fused uncertainty geometry and Figure 4 turns it into a token cutoff example. Figure 5 is the main performance/efficiency headline linked to Tables 1–4, while Appendix Figures 6–7 and Tables 5–8 extend response-length, ALFWorld, sensitivity, staleness, hyperparameter, and reward-decomposition checks. The PDF’s §5 prose incorrectly calls the main stability/efficiency panels “Figure 7”, although the main composite is Figure 5 and Figure 7 is the appendix ALFWorld figure.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use an italic Figure/Table label followed by sentence-style prose. Figure 1, Figure 3, Figure 4, and Figure 5 state a mechanism or finding; Figure 2 and Figure 7 are terse setup-only captions. Most captions omit sample denominators and uncertainty definitions; Figure 5 names bands/curves only indirectly and Figure 7 does not define its encodings.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables use compact booktabs or partial-grid rules, bold proposed/best cells, and grouped rows. Tables 1–2 use multi-level benchmark headers; Tables 3–4 and 6–8 use compact outcome columns; Table 5 uses italic lifecycle group rows. Units and uncertainty notation are inconsistently explicit, especially in Tables 1 and 8.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figures 2–4 map equations and control points to TTI/TDS; Figure 5 and Table 1 test the headline performance and efficiency claim; Tables 3–4 delete core modules or replace them with alternative controls; Table 8 decomposes reward outcomes to connect the mechanism to fine-grained task progress.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figure 5’s token/turn efficiency is extended by Appendix Figure 6’s response-length/clipping settings and Figure 7’s ALFWorld replication. Table 5 records all task configurations, Table 6 tests pipeline staleness, Table 7 selects α, and Table 8 decomposes WebShop reward components.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF object fonts are stable Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern across captions and tables, with bold/italic hierarchy preserved. Rasterized plots use approximate Times-like labels and occasional monospaced token text, so small-size and math rendering vary across figures even though the paper-level caption style is coherent.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/orange commonly distinguish GiGPO and T²PO in Figures 5 and 7; red/blue/purple encode seed or maximum-length settings in Figures 1 and 6. However, Figure 3 uses three independent scalar colormaps, Figure 4 changes color semantics by panel, and tables are grayscale. Color roles are locally understandable but not globally standardized.

most_reusable_patterns: Failure triptych: align an outcome curve with internal diagnostics and a bounded highlighted failure interval.
Method interface: connect rollout states to token-level and turn-level decisions using matched boxes, direct labels, and arrows.
Efficiency composite: combine outcome, token-budget distribution/success ratio, and interaction turns with explicit budget reference lines.
Mechanism-to-evidence chain: follow a metric contour comparison with a signal trajectory and one executable token-level example.
highest_value_objects: Figure 5, because it puts task performance and token/turn cost on one decision surface.
Figure 2, because the four-box interface is the clearest bridge from equations to implementation and has the only verified public visual asset.
Table 1, because it joins WebShop and ALFWorld headline outcomes across prompting, SFT, and two RL backbones.
Figure 3 plus Figure 4, because they make the fused uncertainty signal and TTI trigger mechanistically inspectable.
failure_patterns: Uncertainty, seed aggregation, run counts, and denominators are frequently omitted from captions and tables.
Table 8 mixes decimal fractions with percentage-like reward values, weakening direct comparison.
Table 2’s MuSiQue prose claim conflicts with the displayed values.
The main-results prose contains a Figure 7 cross-reference for the Figure 5 stability/efficiency content.
Rasterized small legends, token text, and color-only scalar encodings reduce accessibility and auditability.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a failure-to-mechanism-to-efficiency narrative: diagnose unstable exploration, diagram two uncertainty controls, visualize their signal/cutoff logic, then validate performance and resource efficiency with grouped benchmarks, ablations, and appendix stress tests.
